Parameter estimation that minimizes the sum of squared residuals.
Observed value minus model-predicted value.
Minimize ‖b − Ax‖²; solution satisfies the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb.
Aᵀr = 0: residuals are orthogonal to the columns of A; with an intercept they sum to zero.
R² = 1 − SSR/SST; check residual patterns for curvature, saturation or outliers.
Read unknowns only inside the standards' range; uncertainty grows away from the mean.
pₙ₊₁ = M pₙ; with column vectors each column of M sums to one.
Mπ = π (eigenvalue 1); for two states π_A = (B→A)/(A→B + B→A).
Deviation shrinks by λ₂ per step; for two states λ₂ = 1 − (A→B) − (B→A).
Switching depends only on the current state; history effects need extra states.
Rank = number of independent columns = dimension of the column space; null space = {x : Ax = 0}; rank + nullity = number of columns.
Ax = b is solvable only if b is in the column space; if a solution x₀ exists, all solutions are x₀ + null space, so unknowns with a null component are not identifiable.
The solution of smallest length is orthogonal to the null space; it is a convention, not a measurement.
An intercept plus a full set of indicators is rank deficient; drop one column or impose a constraint; near-dependence is the practical version.
p = (a·b/a·a) a; the residual r = b − p is perpendicular to a; ‖b‖² = ‖p‖² + ‖r‖².
q₁ = a₁/‖a₁‖; v₂ = a₂ − (q₁·a₂)q₁; q₂ = v₂/‖v₂‖; a zero v₂ means a₂ was dependent.
A = QR with R upper triangular; solve Rx = Qᵀb by back-substitution; the residual norm is √(‖b‖² − ‖Qᵀb‖²).
AᵀA squares the condition number; QR does not form it, so it is the stable way to solve least-squares problems.
A real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors: A = QΛQᵀ, with trace = sum and determinant = product of the eigenvalues.
For [[a, b], [b, d]], θ = ½ atan2(2b, a − d) gives a dominant axis, modulo 180°, when the eigenvalues differ. A repeated eigenvalue has no unique dominant axis.
xᵀAx = a₁₁x₁² + 2a₁₂x₁x₂ + a₂₂x₂²; over unit vectors it ranges from λ_min to λ_max; positive definite means all eigenvalues are positive.
For a covariance matrix C and a unit vector w the variance is wᵀCw; the maximum is λ_max along its eigenvector; the total variance is the trace.

For an m × n matrix, A = UΣVᵀ with orthogonal U (m × m), V (n × n) and rectangular diagonal Σ (m × n). Positive σ² are the nonzero eigenvalues shared by AᵀA and AAᵀ; rank counts nonzero σ. Orthogonal factors can include reflections.
Eckart–Young: keep the k largest terms; the error in the Frobenius norm is √(sum of the dropped σ²); ‖A‖²_F = Σ σ².
A rank-k approximation of an m × n matrix needs k(m + n + 1) numbers instead of mn; saves storage only if k(m + n + 1) < mn; usefulness also requires acceptable error.
A very small last singular value means near rank deficiency; For full column rank, σ₁/σ_min is the 2-norm condition number; rank deficiency makes inversion nonunique.
For invertible A, κ₂ = σ_max/σ_min; fixed-A relative signal errors have a worst-case multiplier κ₂.
Small residual means a close fit to supplied data; poorly conditioned columns can still give large parameter errors.
In a singular direction ridge multiplies the unregularized coefficient by σ²/(σ² + α). This introduces bias.
Condition numbers and penalties depend on coordinate scales. Report units, scaling, calibration uncertainty and tuning.
For n sample rows, subtract column means and use C = ZᵀZ/(n − 1). Uncentered SVD answers a different question.
Score t = z·q; rank-one centered reconstruction is tq. Add the training mean to recover original coordinates.
Covariance PCA preserves the stated units; standardized PCA uses a correlation matrix and weights each variable to unit variance.
Explained variance is descriptive. Assess confounding and fit preprocessing on training data only.
For independent signal noise s²I, singular-direction parameter variance is s²/σ_i².
Averaging n independent signal pairs divides covariance by n. Shared calibration offsets do not average away.
Compare geometry using calibrated gains and a stated noise covariance; exercise the weak direction.
State units, matrix, noise assumptions, singular values, parameter uncertainty, estimator convention and independent validation.
Compute √[mean of squared Euclidean errors], using an independent reference; mean error can cancel while RMSE is large.
The lab pairs opposite errors deliberately. Its independent-noise uncertainty calculation uses a separate stated model.
An invertible two-equation model fits two noisy signals exactly; the residual does not certify displacement accuracy.
Compare weak gains, calibrated units and error covariance. Validate new reference displacements in the weak direction.
C(A) and N(Aᵀ) lie in Rᵐ; C(Aᵀ) and N(A) lie in Rⁿ.

cards.front: Rank and nullity in both dimensions
cards.back: rank(A)+dim N(A)=n; rank(A)+dim N(Aᵀ)=m for an m×n matrix.

cards.front: Consistency from the left null space
cards.back: Ax=b is consistent exactly when yᵀb=0 for every y in N(Aᵀ), equivalently b lies in C(A).
At a least-squares fit, r=b−Ax̂ lies in N(Aᵀ), so Aᵀr=0 and r is perpendicular to the column space.
|det A| is the factor by which x ↦ Ax scales area or volume; the sign records whether orientation is preserved or reversed.
det A ≠ 0 exactly when elimination gives n nonzero pivots, the null space is {0} and the columns are independent.
Exchanging rows flips the sign, scaling a row scales det, adding a multiple of another row leaves det unchanged; det(cA) = cⁿ det A.
A tiny determinant can belong to a well-conditioned matrix (0.1I) and rescaling changes det without changing the condition number.
x̂ solves least squares exactly when the residual is orthogonal to every column: Aᵀ(b − A x̂) = 0.
The singular values of A are the square roots of the eigenvalues of AᵀA; κ₂(A) is the largest over the smallest.
If every other eigenvalue of a column-stochastic T has magnitude below 1, p_k approaches the stationary vector with eigenvalue 1.

cards.front: Why does a zero leading entry not prove singularity?
cards.back: A row interchange may provide a nonzero pivot; invertibility depends on the complete map, not one entry in one row ordering.

cards.front: Why can an invertible coordinate change fail to preserve the ordinary coordinate norm?
cards.back: A nonorthogonal basis has a nonidentity Gram matrix; carry that metric to compare the same physical length.

cards.front: Which transformation represents a linear map in a new basis?
cards.back: S inverse A S when x=Sz; substituting into a scalar quadratic form instead gives S transpose A S.

cards.front: What should a transformation proof identify first?
cards.back: The object represented—equation system, linear map, scalar form, metric or functional—and the coordinates of its inputs and outputs.

cards.front: Why can a repeated eigenvalue fail to give a diagonalization?
cards.back: The eigenspace may have too few independent eigenvectors to form an invertible eigenvector matrix.

cards.front: What term is lost by replacing a defective matrix power with lambda to the power n times the identity?
cards.back: The polynomial-in-n coupling from the nilpotent part; it can dominate finite-time behavior even when the eventual state decays.

cards.front: How can a matrix-exponential formula be checked independently?
cards.back: Verify its initial identity and derivative equation, or solve the triangular component equations in sequence.

cards.front: Which matrix controls the instantaneous Euclidean norm derivative?
cards.back: The symmetric part of the generator; negative real parts of generator eigenvalues alone are a weaker asymptotic statement.

cards.front: Why state ambient spaces with subspace dimensions?
cards.back: Row/null spaces belong to input space while column/left-null spaces belong to output space; rectangular maps distinguish those dimensions.

cards.front: Why does minimum norm not identify every physical input component?
cards.back: It chooses one representative among inputs with identical outputs; null-space directions remain unobserved by the supplied map.

cards.front: How does a left-null vector certify inconsistency?
cards.back: It annihilates every Ax; a nonzero pairing with b proves b cannot equal Ax for any input.

cards.front: What should a least-squares proof retain beyond fitted coefficients?
cards.back: The declared inner product/objective, residual orthogonality, uniqueness conditions and an independent projection or factorization check.

cards.front: Why does a positive-definite quadratic have a unique stationary minimum?
cards.back: Its shifted objective difference is half a strictly positive quadratic form for every nonzero displacement from the stationary point.

cards.front: Why track an inner product in projections and coordinate changes?
cards.back: Orthogonality and lengths depend on its metric; a numerical array alone does not identify which geometry is being represented.

cards.front: Why is the scalar spectral-radius power not the entire state history?
cards.back: A nonorthogonal or defective structure can add coupling and polynomial factors that matter at finite times.

cards.front: How should a discrete transient maximum be checked?
cards.back: Compare the exact sequence or successive-term ratios and neighboring integer steps, separately for each specified observable.

cards.front: Can one coordinate rise while the Euclidean state norm falls?
cards.back: Yes. Component transfer can coexist with a negative total norm derivative; state the exact observable being discussed.

cards.front: What does the pseudoinverse choose in an underdetermined consistent system?
cards.back: The minimum-norm exact representative under the specified inner products; it does not observe an input null-space component.

cards.front: Why can a retained-energy criterion miss an important inverse response?
cards.back: The requested right-hand side may align with a dropped singular direction even when that mode contributes little to total matrix energy.

cards.front: Does a regularized solution create information in a null direction?
cards.back: No. Its penalty selects a convention and trades fit against input size; the unobserved direction remains unobserved by A.
